n: Paul’s deepest longing and prayer is that his fellow Israelites will be saved. His teaching flows from love, not resentment.

f.w: my heart's desire and prayer

n: He can testify that they are zealous for God — but their zeal isn’t guided by true understanding. Sincerity alone isn’t enough.

f.w: a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge

n: Not understanding the righteousness God gives, they tried to set up their own, and wouldn’t submit to God’s way.

f.w: establish their own righteousness

n: Christ is the “end” of the law — its goal and fulfillment — bringing righteousness to everyone who believes. The law of Moses pointed to him all along.

f.w: end
Christ is the end of the law

n: Moses described law-based righteousness: whoever does these things will live by them. That requires perfect obedience no one can achieve alone.

f.w: the man which doeth those things shall live by them

n: But faith-based righteousness says: Don’t ask, “Who will go up to heaven?” — as if we had to bring Christ down ourselves. He has already come.

f.w: Who shall ascend into heaven?

n: Or, “Who will go down into the deep?” — as if we had to raise Christ from the dead. He has already risen.

f.w: Who shall descend into the deep?

n: Instead, the message is close to you — in your mouth and in your heart. This is the word of faith we preach. Salvation isn’t far off or impossible to reach.

f.w: The word is nigh thee
nigh

n: If you openly declare that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved. Faith and testimony go together.

f.w: confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus
God hath raised him from the dead

n: With the heart we believe and are made righteous; with the mouth we declare our faith and are saved.
Scripture says whoever believes in him will not be put to shame.

f.w: Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed

n: There is no distinction between Jew and Greek. The same Lord is Lord of all and generously blesses everyone who calls on him.

f.w: there is no difference between the Jew and the Greek
rich unto all

n: As Joel prophesied, everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.

f.w: whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved

n: But how can people call on someone they don’t believe in? How can they believe without hearing? How can they hear without someone preaching? A chain of steps.

f.w: how shall they hear without a preacher?

n: And how can anyone preach unless they are sent? Isaiah praised the beautiful feet of messengers bringing good news. Authorized sending matters.

f.w: except they be sent
How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace

n: But not everyone accepted the good news. Isaiah asked, “Lord, who has believed our message?”

f.w: Lord, who hath believed our report?

n: So faith comes from hearing, and hearing comes through the word of God (many manuscripts read “the word of Christ”). Faith grows as we hear and receive God’s word.

f.w: faith cometh by hearing

n: Haven’t they heard? Indeed they have — Paul applies a psalm about creation’s voice to the gospel spreading worldwide.

f.w: their sound went into all the earth

n: Didn’t Israel understand? Moses foretold that God would make Israel jealous through a “nation that is not a nation” — the Gentiles.

f.w: I will provoke you to jealousy by them that are no people

n: Isaiah boldly says that God was found by people who weren’t looking for him — the Gentiles.

f.w: I was found of them that sought me not

n: But to Israel God says: all day long I have held out my hands to a disobedient and stubborn people. God’s arms remain open — an image the Book of Mormon repeats often.

f.w: All day long I have stretched forth my hands
gainsaying
